result.title: E5-PATH: delayed-entry long after the fade. A pre-registered entry-timing x horizon grid on the frozen G2_RET30 flag (crypto primary, US secondary) with matched controls under each plan
result.angle: STRUCTURE/EXECUTION: keep the frozen detector, change only WHEN the long is entered (open of t+1, t+2, t+3, t+6, t+11) and HOW LONG it is held (5, 10, 20 sessions). The grid is simultaneously a tradeable-plan search and the first pre-registered post-flag return path map beyond t+5, measured against matched controls executed under the identical plan.
result.thesis: Every long-side statistic in the repo stops at t+5 and every long entry is at t+1: E2 found that buying the next open after a +30% day loses (US -3.65% vs -0.60%; crypto -1.90% vs +1.42% on 2023; median 5-session return about -10% vs 0% matched), and E3/E4 showed the fade is real and the right tail is fat. Nobody has measured what the flagged names do AFTER the fade. Hypothesis (mechanism): the +30% day carries information about further repricing (the flag's E30 lift of 5.4x/4.6x vs matched is validated detection), and the t+1..t+5 fade is a transient positioning unwind (chasers and day-traders exiting) rather than a reversal of the information; once the unwind completes, flagged names drift up relative to matched names, so a long entered at the open of t+3, t+6 or t+11 and held 5-20 sessions earns a positive net return that beats matched random entries under the same plan, in every discovery year. The rival mechanism (lottery/MAX-effect decay: names with extreme daily returns underperform for the following month; dilution and pump-and-dump structure in sub-$5 names) predicts every delayed cell is negative versus matched and the loss keeps compounding with horizon. The grid distinguishes the two with one frozen protocol: the lag-1 cells reproduce the known fade; the lag-6/lag-11 cells test whether the names stop losing once the unwind is over. On crypto the entry open is the prior close (median |open/prev-1| = 0.04% pre-2024), so the test is a clean close-to-close path; on US it includes the real opening gap.
result.why_not_already_falsified: E1/E2 traded only entry t+1 (close on IDX, open on US/crypto) and exit t+5; E2's detection statistics (r5, r5max, lead to peak) stop at t+5. E3 (IDX, 108 plans) varied the entry RULE inside s+1..s+3 with close entries and holds 2/3/5; it never delayed an unconditional entry beyond s+1 and never held beyond 5 (research/E3/protocol.json plans; e3.harness_config hard-codes entry_lag=1). E4 (crypto, 144+288 plans) was the SHORT side with holds 1/2/3/5; by symmetry its reference rows (E4/CRYPTO/discovery/plans.csv G2_RET30|fixed1|fixed|h1..h5: short +1.36%/+0.84%/-0.09%/-102% with 2021 negative and 2022 positive) imply the lag-1 LONG cells at h<=5, not any delayed entry or any horizon beyond t+5. US_BREAKOUT_v1 used a different signal (60-session breakout) with a 5% stop and a 5-session time exit. PR #5 (E3_US_RETENTION_v1, unrun) conditions on close(t+1) >= close(t) and enters at open t+2 hold 5 on US only; its unconditional arm B equals exactly one cell of this grid (US lag-2/h5) and its arm C is not in this grid. Signal family: unchanged (G2_RET30 copied verbatim, as E3 copied E1 and E4 copied E2). Information source: unchanged (price/volume only). What is new: the entry-timing axis (t+2..t+11) and the horizon axis (10 and 20 sessions), in both open-entry markets, with the harness's matched controls under each plan. Regime-conditioned longs were considered and rejected as the primary idea: the existing 2023 numbers already quasi-falsify a BTC-bull-gated long on crypto (E2 crypto 2023 unconditioned long -1.90% vs +1.42% matched while E4 v2's BEAR-regime shorts on the same flags were -1.50%, i.e. the bear-regime longs were roughly flat and the bull-regime longs carried the loss), and a regime chosen after seeing 2021-vs-2022 is the design pattern that failed in E4 v2.

protocol.family: G2_RET30 (MOONSHOT_E2 family, moonshot_g.py; the frozen selected detector for US and CRYPTO), long side only, code copied verbatim into idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py exactly as moonshot_e3.py copied moonshot_e1.py; no threshold, feature or regime change; candidate rule id E5_CAND_G2_RET30 (hold 5, no plan) for discovery, MOONSHOT_E5_D1 after the freeze
detectors: G2_RET30 (one detector; G1/G7/G10 and any _BEAR/_BULL variant deliberately excluded to keep the cell count at 15 per market)
protocol.plans: entries: fixed open entry at session s+k for k in {1,2,3,6,11} (protocol JSON entries [["fixed",1],["fixed",2],["fixed",3],["fixed",6],["fixed",11]], the existing E3 schema where the second element is the lag for a fixed entry, matching ExecConfig.plan and plan_text 'buy at ... session s + {w}'); exits: fixed only (close of entry+h, rolled forward while untraded, EXIT_DATA_END at the last traded close if the name leaves the data, INCOMPLETE if the target is beyond the window); holds h in {5,10,20}; 5 x 1 x 3 = 15 cells per market, 30 discovery runs plus 2 reproduce runs plus the US stress reruns of any admissible US cell plus at most 2 validation runs. The lag-1/h5 cell is the reference row (E2's plan; its 2023 outcome has been seen) and is NOT selectable. Conditional entries/exits (confirm, pullback, stop_ref, first_down) are excluded: E3 showed stops do not help the long side and conditional open entries exist only on the unmerged E4 branch.
markets: CRYPTO (primary): panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z (sha 3dc12749...), on disk; Binance spot USDT, 683 pairs incl. 190 delisted; entry at the UTC-day open (= prior close); notional $5,000; fees 0.1%+0.1% slippage per side plus the 0.1% tier (profile CRYPTO); fill model A (10% of entry-session volume, as E2/E4); ca_mode adjusted; overlap skip; data_end_exit last_close

US (secondary): panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (sha 8d3b7ce4..., causal-close-v2, 4,878 names, read_through 2023-12-29), on disk; units 'panel' (split-adjusted returns are internally consistent across a trade window), quarantine 'none' (repair_v3 showed name quarantine is outcome-correlated), fill model A, notional $5,000, profile cost tiers per side (1.5% <$1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above, plus SEC fee); STRESS RULE: a US cell is admissible only if it is still admissible when every trade is charged an additional flat 1.5% per side on top of its tier (the largest possible unit-induced tier error is 1.45% per side; 2020-22 units are unverified); survivor-only universe is a declared, uncorrected flattering bias for longs
protocol.discovery_period: 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (E2's discovery window for G2_RET30; in-sample for the detector, as PR #5's addendum notes, which is why only PLANS are searched and the detector is never touched); per-year rule applies to 2020 (H2 only), 2021, 2022
protocol.validation_period: 2023-01-01..2023-12-31, one recorded harness run (results.write_run) per market of MOONSHOT_E5_D1 with the frozen cell; the harness slices the study market at `end` (backtest.run L275/L300) so no 2024 session is ever loaded; pass if scored >= 100, avg net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (E3's validation rule). Declared caveat: the lag-1/h5 outcomes on 2023 are already known from E2 (both markets) and US 2023 has been replayed many times (PR #5 calls it 'spent'); a US pass is therefore one-year evidence on previously replayed data and a crypto pass is one-year evidence on a year whose lag-1/h5 outcome was seen. Consequence of a pass: a new paper policy version may score the validated delayed plan prospectively from decisions the ledger already records (no new scans needed, no real orders); consequence of a fail: the unconditional long plan family for G2_RET30 is exhausted at every entry timing to t+11 and every horizon to t+31 in that market.
protocol.admissibility: On discovery, per market, per cell (E3's rule verbatim plus two additions): scored >= 200; average net return > 0; one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (200 draws, seed 20261007/+1, floor 0.005); average net return > 0 in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored trades (by signal year, as backtest.by_year keys it); [new] US only: still admissible under the +1.5%/side stress costs; [new] the lag-1/h5 reference cell is excluded from selection. Selection: the admissible cell with the highest average net return, ties by more scored then grid order; at most one cell per market; frozen into moonshot_e5.SELECTED (per-market tuple like moonshot_g.SELECTED) and committed before any validation statistic. Precondition stage (as E3/E4): re-run the recorded E2 trading runs on the chosen panels with their recorded configs and record REPRODUCED/DEVIATES before any grid number: CRYPTO 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 (same panel sha 3dc12749, expected exact), US 20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (R1c: panel 8d3b7ce4, units panel, quarantine none, fill A, 1,101 scored, -3.745% vs -0.624%). Descriptive, non-decision outputs frozen in the same protocol: (a) path.csv per market: mean and median of open(t+1)->close(t+j) for j = 1..21 over the attempted lag-1/h20 signals and over the deterministic matched-control tickers (controls.matched_draws re-derived with the same seed), before costs, split by discovery year; (b) an equal-notional ledger of all scored trades of each cell aggregated by exit session (cumulative P&L, max drawdown) for the rule and for the pooled matched draws, labelled descriptive. Multiplicity note recorded in the protocol: 14 selectable cells per market, highly correlated (same flags); the per-year positivity rule and the single validation are the guards, as in E3/E4.
protocol.matched_controls: Harness controls v2 exactly as every recorded run computes them: for each attempted signal, 200 names drawn on the same session from names where the rule was evaluable, matched on price_band, liquidity quintile, volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile and listing_age at the signal session (market_cap only where listed_shares exist; relaxed from the last feature until >= 5 names match), executed under the identical ExecConfig including the entry lag and hold (backtest.run L333-344 passes exec_cfg to _baseline; overlap-skip at L304 uses s + entry_lag). Same-session uniform baseline recorded as secondary. One-sided p = (1 + #draws with mean >= observed)/201.
protocol.costs_model: CRYPTO: 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side plus the profile's 0.1% tier; no carry on longs; liquidation/jump_ratio not applicable (long, 1x, no leverage); redenomination jumps are the same risk E2 accepted (LUNA/NFP spike rows already dropped by the panel). US: SEC fee on sale + price-tier cost per side from the adjusted price, plus the pre-registered +1.5%/side stress rerun as an admissibility condition. Both: fixed notional $5,000, whole units, fill model A (10% of entry-session volume, labelled ex-post as in E2/E4), no price impact, no dividends, daily bars only (no intraday path; irrelevant here because the plan has no stop).

data_needed: idx-signals/data/panel/panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz (on disk, manifest committed, sha 3dc12749...); the run passes end=2022-12-31 / 2023-12-31 explicitly so the 2024+ rows in the file are never sliced into the study market
results/runs/20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 and results/runs/20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 summary.json configs (on HEAD) for the precondition reproduce stage
No network pulls, no new panels, no registry; no holdout rows read at any stage
code_changes: idxsig/backtest.py resolve_plan (L87-92) and run (L231-250): carry the entry lag of a fixed plan into ExecConfig.entry_lag (for entry_rule == 'fixed', entry_lag = the plan's entry_window; explicit RunConfig.entry_window/--entry-lag take precedence; default stays 1 so every recorded run reproduces unchanged). ExecConfig.plan (execution.py L127-130) and ENTRY_TEXT['fixed'] already encode the lag as entry_window, so plan ids ('G2_RET30|fixed6|fixed|h10') and plan_text need no change. Add tests in tests/test_plans.py: a ('fixed', 3) plan on an open-entry market enters at the open of s+3, the matched baseline shares the lag, overlap-skip uses s+3, reproduce-equivalence of a lag-1 run.

idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py: verbatim copy of moonshot_g.py's features/family_flags/FAMILY (the module may import nothing from the package; passes rules/audit.py), RULE_ID 'MOONSHOT_E5_D1', VERSION 'v1', CANDIDATES = ('G2_RET30',), SELECTED = None until the freeze then a per-market mapping {'CRYPTO': ('G2_RET30','fixed',k,'fixed',h), 'US': (...)} (pattern: moonshot_g.SELECTED per market + moonshot_e3.selected_plan), selected_plan() -> {'entry_rule':'fixed','entry_window':k,'exit_rule':'fixed'}, rules() emitting E5_CAND_G2_RET30 (hold 5, no plan) and MOONSHOT_E5_D1 (hold h, plan) with 'Selected: ...; plan: ...' in the rule text so the rule hash covers the plan; register the module in idxsig/rules/__init__.py registry() tuple (L61-64).

idxsig/e5.py modelled on e4.py (which already generalises e3.py to markets): protocol() reading research/E5/protocol.json with sha256 stamped into every stage output; plan_grid via e3.plan_grid (entries list carries the lag); harness_config(proto, market, rule_id, period, plan) building RunConfig with entry_lag = plan['entry_window'] for fixed entries, market-specific notional/fees/units/quarantine from the protocol; run_reproduce (the two E2 runs named in protocol['precondition'], REPRODUCED/DEVIATES as e3.run_reproduce); run_discovery (15 cells per market through backtest.run with the signal cache; plans.csv, reference_summary.json for lag-1/h5, summary.json with admissible flags, selected_tuple and freeze instruction; US stress reruns of admissible cells via RunConfig fee_buy/fee_sell += 0.015 recorded as plans_stress.csv); admissibility = e3.admissibility + stress condition + reference-cell exclusion; select = e3.select over selectable rows; run_validation requiring moonshot_e5.SELECTED[market] == discovery selected_tuple, one write_run-recorded run on the validation period, result.json with passed and consequence (e3.run_validation pattern).

idxsig/e5.py descriptive stage (frozen in the protocol, non-decision): path.csv per market from the lag-1/h20 discovery run: mean/median open(t+1)->close(t+j), j=1..21, for attempted signals and for the matched-control tickers re-derived deterministically with controls.features + controls.matched_draws(seed 20261007+1); ledger.csv per cell: equal-notional cumulative P&L and max drawdown by exit session for the rule and the pooled matched draws (from trades.csv.gz and a per-draw trade frame the driver keeps in memory, not from random_draws.csv which holds only per-draw aggregates).

idxsig/cli.py: subcommands e5-reproduce / e5-discovery [--accept-deviation] / e5-validation --market CRYPTO|US, refusing a dirty idxsig/ tree exactly like e3-*/e4-* (cli.py L326/L345/L379 pattern); for US/CRYPTO the driver sets start/end from protocol.json periods (never the panel's source_boundary), and if PR #7 is merged first the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard (e4 branch backtest.py L85, L296-300) refuses any mistake in code.

research/E5/protocol.json + PROTOCOL.md (frozen, committed, sha recorded before any statistic; research/ is append-only under tools/check_append_only.py); tests/test_e5.py: grid has 15 cells per market, lag mapping, admissibility including the stress and reference-cell rules, selection excludes lag-1/h5, validation refuses when SELECTED mismatches.

Out of scope until a validation passes (and then a new POLICY_ID): a paper-score-v4 scorer for a delayed plan reading the DECISION records already in paper/ledger.jsonl (entry at the open of session+k, exit at close+h), so prospective evidence accrues without new scans.
result.falsifier: Discovery: in BOTH markets, no selectable cell (any lag in {2,3,6,11} with any hold, or lag 1 with hold 10/20) is admissible, i.e. none has scored >= 200, avg net > 0, p < 0.05 vs matched random under the same plan, avg net > 0 in each discovery year with >= 50 scored (and, for US, survives +1.5%/side). That result kills the hypothesis that the fade is a transient unwind around retained information: the flagged names keep losing versus matched names at every entry timing to t+11 and every horizon to t+31, which is the lottery/MAX-decay mechanism, and the unconditional long plan family for G2_RET30 is closed. Validation: if a cell is selected and the single 2023 run of MOONSHOT_E5_D1 shows scored < 100, or avg net <= 0, or p >= 0.05 vs matched, the family is exhausted for that market (E3/E4's consequence_if_failed), with no second design pass on 2023. A specific pre-stated pattern that would also count as falsified even with a stray admissible cell: the path map showing mean rule-minus-matched still declining from j=6 to j=21 in every discovery year (persistent decay) while the admissible cell's edge is confined to 2021.
risks: Prior is against the hypothesis: the academic MAX/lottery effect and E2's lag-1 losses both predict negative delayed cells; the experiment is more likely to close the long side than to open it (that is still decisive information, see expected_information_value).

Contamination declared: the lag-1/h5 cell's 2023 outcomes were seen in E2 (both markets) and E4 v2 saw 2023 crypto short outcomes; the delayed cells are correlated with them through the same flags. Mitigation: the reference cell is excluded from selection, the protocol is frozen before any delayed number exists, selection is on discovery only; US 2023 is 'spent' per PR #5's addendum, so a US pass is weaker than a crypto pass and the clean confirmation is prospective scoring from the ledger.

Multiplicity: 14 selectable cells per market; E3's p < 0.05 is kept for comparability; the per-year rule and the single validation are the guards; the orchestrator may prefer p < 0.01 on discovery (pre-register either, not both).

Sample attrition at long horizons: hold-20 cells lose the last ~31 sessions of each period to INCOMPLETE and overlap-skip removes consecutive-day re-flags of the same name; crypto 2023 (298 flags) may fall below 100 scored at h20, which is a fail 'for the right reason' (E4 v2 regime_note pattern), not a reason to relax.

US data: 2020-22 split units unverified (cost tiers may be mis-stated by up to 1.45%/side, hence the stress rule); survivor-only universe flatters longs by an unknown amount; opening gaps are real on US (36% of days > 1%) so US lag-k entries pay a gap the crypto cells do not.

Crypto data: 49 pre-2024 pairs stop trading > 20 sessions before 2023-12-31 (EXIT_DATA_END at the last traded close, as E2 accepted); pairs Binance dropped from exchangeInfo entirely are absent; redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops only (no jump_ratio on the long side).

Harness plumbing: resolve_plan must carry the lag without changing any recorded run's reproduction; the precondition reproduce stage catches a regression before any grid number (E3's DEVIATES precedent shows the harness records, not hides, such drift).

Per-trade averages with fixed notional: a positive cell could rest on a few large winners (fat right tail); the descriptive equal-notional ledger and max drawdown are reported but are not decision criteria, so a pass remains 'one year under assumed costs and daily-bar fills' and never prospective performance.
result.directive_compliance: Holdout: never read; both panels contain 2024+ rows but backtest.run slices the study market at the protocol's end (2022-12-31 / 2023-12-31; backtest.py L275/L300), the driver takes start/end from protocol.json periods (never source_boundary), and merging PR #7 first adds the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO. No re-tune: G2_RET30's code is copied verbatim (the E3/E4 method); nothing in the rule, its threshold, features or regime changes; only the execution plan (entry lag, hold) is searched, on discovery only, and the one cell whose 2023 outcome is known (lag-1/h5) is barred from selection. No manufactured results: this proposal states no expected return; the cells' values are unknown until run; the precondition reproduce stage must pass or be recorded as DEVIATES before any grid number; every stage output carries the protocol sha, panel sha and rule sha (e3/e4 _stamp pattern); results are written by write_run into append-only, hash-verified directories. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json and PROTOCOL.md are committed before any statistic (run refuses a dirty tree; research/ frozen by tools/check_append_only.py); admissibility, selection, the reference-cell exclusion, the US stress rule, the validation pass rule and both consequences are fixed in the JSON; the descriptive path map and ledger are declared non-decision in advance. No real orders, no ASTRA/production change; a pass can only create a new paper policy version that scores the plan prospectively from ledger decisions. This session was read-only: no file was created or modified and no harness run or network pull was started.
result.expected_information_value: Either way the repo gains its first pre-registered, matched-controlled post-flag return path beyond t+5 (15 windows per market spanning t+1..t+31, by year, under a frozen protocol), which pins the mechanism the repo currently labels 'plausible, not demonstrated': if the lag-6/lag-11 cells sit at or above matched while lag-1 cells are negative, the fade is a transient unwind of an informational move and a delayed long is a candidate plan with a clear prospective scoring path from the existing ledger decisions; if every delayed cell stays below matched and the gap widens with horizon, the flagged population decays persistently (lottery/MAX structure), the long side of G2_RET30 is closed at every entry timing and horizon (not just t+1/t+5), PR #5's retention arm inherits a strong negative prior (its arm B is a cell here), and the remaining structural question moves to the horizon of the short side, which E4 never tested beyond 5 sessions and which would be a new protocol. The grid also measures, for the first time, how much of the known 5-session loss is the t+1 open gap (US lag-1 vs crypto lag-1, where the open is the prior close) versus later drift, and gives the descriptive aggregate P&L/drawdown shape of equal-notional ledgers versus pooled matched draws that the 'portfolio-level' question needs before anyone builds a capital-constrained control arm.
